title: Passed pawns: the rule of the square
summary: Count the race with one glance: can the king catch the pawn?
body:
Draw a square from the passed pawn to its promotion rank (the pawn's distance to promotion is the side).

- If the defending king can **step into the square** on its move, it catches the pawn.
- If not, the pawn promotes on its own - just **push**.
- Count before you trade into a pawn ending; one tempo decides it.

examples.prompt: White to move. Can the black king catch your a-pawn?
examples.explain: After a6 the black king is outside the square a6-a8-c8-c6 and can't get in. Just push: a7 and a8=Q.

examples.prompt: White to move. Stop the h-pawn.
examples.explain: Kd2 steps into the square d1-h1-h5-d5, so your king reaches the pawn in time. Any other move is too slow.
